tools.name: market_signals
tools.description: Aggregate, keyless market statistics: salary percentiles (p25/p50/p75, annualised EUR) and time-to-fill (days) by job family x country x seniority, plus listing/company/open/closed counts for that segment. Every percentile is suppressed (returned null, never a guess) below a minimum sample size -- n

findings.detail: Description of "search_jobs" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "sponsor_lookup" is 3311 chars, far longer than this server's median (651). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: coverage, changes_since · Private data: search_jobs, get_job, company_hiring, market_signals, coverage, changes_since, job_status, sponsor_lookup · Public sink: job_status, sponsor_lookup · Destructive: changes_since.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: coverage, changes_since · Private data: search_jobs, get_job, company_hiring, market_signals, coverage, changes_since, job_status, sponsor_lookup · Public sink: job_status, sponsor_lookup · Destructive: changes_since

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_jobs" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
